world: 04 — Pulse (reference pole: blood-donation.com). The lab's pop/journey lane: a click-through hand-rolled FSM titled "WHAT HAPPENS WHEN YOU PRESS A BUTTON?" — one click's life told in five stations (PRESS → SIGNAL → SPRING → SETTLE → SHIP) across a 48-unit filleted toy machine hall. Zero scroll anywhere: the page itself is the button.
policy: Dual-mode, diegetic — both grounds already exist inside the reference (red poster over a plum hall; plum #3d3c47 is its own measured secondary ground), so modes deepen the pole instead of diluting it. DAY = the pole verbatim: poster/curtain red #e5262c, hall clearColor 0x4b4a53, body background #4b4a53. NIGHT = the secondary ground promoted: poster/curtain plum #3d3c47, hall clearColor 0x302c35, body #302c35; red survives ONLY as accents — the curtain's wave strip, pill fills, the roundel disc, the S1 button cap — and the emissive pulse becomes the hall's literal light source via a night-only point light. The curtain body follows the poster in both themes (it IS the poster layer); at night the red wave strip is what carries red through the reveal. Reads localStorage 'hub-theme' ('day'|'night', prefers-color-scheme default) through a BLOCKING inline <head> script that sets <html data-theme> before first paint (scheme-correct first paint, zero flash); writes back on change. The world's toggle is a 54px mini pushbutton — pressing it enacts the thesis in miniature: 150ms cap-dip, then an 800ms cubic-bezier(0.45,0,0.55,1) cross-fade (the hub's own transition curve from tokens.css — lab continuity), with the 3D lights/materials lerping on the same 800ms clock. Single-mode (total red commitment) was considered and rejected: the reference itself runs two grounds, and a world about state changes earns its own state change. Surface-by-surface night retune is specced per element below (poster, tag cord, hall materials, lights) — nothing is left to improvise.
typecasting: ONE family, total commitment — Outfit variable 300–800 (SIL OFL 1.1, already self-hosted at site/public/fonts/Outfit-Variable.woff2, license at site/public/fonts/licenses/). @font-face: font-family 'Outfit', font-weight 300 800, font-display swap, preloaded in <head> (font/woff2, crossorigin). The measured weight map is law: 800 = titles (poster h1 96px / lh 0.9 / ls −5px / uppercase — the measured band is −4 to −6px; dialog titles 32px / lh 0.95 / ls −1px / uppercase), 700 = buttons (16px, +1.4px tracking, uppercase) and roundel ring text (SVG 12px, +2px), 600 = eyebrows (poster 16px, dialog 13px; both +3.5px tracking, uppercase), 300 = body (18px / lh 1.5; microcopy 13px). Weights 400/500 never appear — enforce with exactly four utility classes (.w800/.w700/.w600/.w300) and no raw font-weight declarations anywhere else. Two-tone stacked headlines via per-line spans ONLY: .line{color:#fff} .line--pink{color:#fdd2d2}; gradients on text are forbidden. All sizes px, zero clamp/vw; exactly two breakpoints — ≤960: h1 72px ls −3.5px, dialog title 28px; ≤800: h1 56px ls −2.5px, body 16px, roundel shrinks 149→96px. SVG-baked lettering (tag label 'ONE CLICK', roundel ring) uses live SVG <text> with the self-hosted font — outlining was the reference's font-delivery insurance; self-hosting gives us the same guarantee for free.

downloads.name: NONE — Kenney Toy Car Kit explicitly ruled out for this world (decision record)

All Pulse geometry is built from Three.js primitives (Lathe/Tube/RoundedBox/Torus/Capsule) — zero downloads

sections.name: State 0 — Poster (the cold open)
sections.spec:
**DOM map** (whole world, z-order): `<canvas id=hall>` z0 · `#diagram` fallback strip z5 (hidden) · `#dots` z10 · `<section id=poster>` (also the curtain) z15 · `<aside id=dialog aria-live=polite>` z20 · `<section id=finale>` z25 (hidden) · `#furniture` z30 (toggle, roundel, tag, exit link). `overflow:hidden` on html/body — this world never scrolls. html/body background: #4b4a53 day / #302c35 night (matches hall clearColor — nothing white can ever flash). Blocking inline <head> script reads localStorage 'hub-theme' → `<html data-theme>` before paint.

**Layout**: poster = fixed full-screen layer filled `#e5262c` (day) / `#3d3c47` (night), transitioned 800ms cubic-bezier(0.45,0,0.55,1). Copy block: absolute, left 96px (≤960: 64px; ≤800: 24px), top 50%, translateY(-50%) — static CSS, GSAP only ever animates its children.

**Copy** (top to bottom):
- Eyebrow, 16px/600/+3.5px/uppercase, white: `THE LAB · WORLD 04 · A GUIDED TOUR`
- H1, 96px/800/lh 0.9/ls −5px/uppercase, three stacked spans (white / pink #fdd2d2 / white): `WHAT HAPPENS` / `WHEN YOU PRESS` / `A BUTTON?`
- Body, 18px/300/lh 1.5, white, max-width 380px, margin-top 32px: `Follow one click through the machine — five stations, sixty-ish milliseconds, one very small hero. No scrolling in here. Just press.`
- CTA pill, margin-top 48px, **h 64px** (the measured poster size; dialogs use 54px), radius 44px, pad 0 32px, 16px/700/+1.4px/uppercase: `PRESS THE BUTTON` — white `::before` fill (inset 0, radius 44, z −1), red text; night: red fill, white text. Hover: `::before` scales to 1.05 in 200ms ease-out — NEVER the button element. Active: `::before` scale 0.97, 60ms.
- Microcopy, 13px/300, white 70%, margin-top 16px: `That press is Station 01. It already counts.`
- `<noscript>` line in body style: `This world is a machine — it needs JavaScript to run.`

**Entrance** (GSAP, delays on the 300ms grid): eyebrow fade 0.6s pulseFade at 0s; h1 lines pop y 40→0 + autoAlpha at 0.3/0.6/0.9s (0.6s each, pulsePop); body+CTA+micro fade 0.6s at 1.2s.

**Exit on press** (the measured 96→144px trick, as transform): h1 `scale 1→1.5` + autoAlpha 0, 0.9s, pulseExit, transformOrigin '0 50%' (grows rightward like the reference's font-size swap), at t=0.3s; eyebrow/body/CTA/micro autoAlpha 0 at t=0 (0.45s pulseExit). Then the curtain runs. Keyboard: Enter/Space triggers START anywhere in poster state. Body gets `data-state` per FSM state for CSS hooks (exit link visibility).

sections.name: The curtain (poster → hall)
sections.spec:
The poster layer itself is the curtain — the measured reveal, used exactly once per run.

**Sequence** (t from CTA press):
- t=0–0.9s: copy exits (previous section).
- t=0.9s: the WebGL hall is already rendering behind (canvas z0, warmed during poster idle at 1 frame / 2s via setTimeout to dodge cold-start hitch; full rAF resumes here). GSAP slides the poster layer `yPercent: 0 → 140` over **2s, ease 'none'** (linear, as measured).
- The curtain's top edge carries the wave: `::after`, absolute, top −127px (1px overlap kills the seam), width 100%, height 128px, background = inline data-URI SVG **512×128** wave strip filled `#e5272c` (the SVG red — the reference's two reds coexist and so do ours), repeat-x; GSAP animates `backgroundPositionX: −512px` per **1s, linear, repeat −1** while the curtain moves. Wave path: `M0,128 L0,64 C42,26 86,26 128,64 S214,102 256,64 S342,26 384,64 S470,102 512,64 L512,128 Z`. The strip stays RED in both themes — it is the accent that carries red through a night reveal.
- t=2.9s: curtain `display:none`; FSM enters `station(1)`: camera is pre-parked at the S1 pose (no travel for S1), the giant button self-presses (cap dips scaleY 0.82 in 150ms, pops back 0.35s pulsePop), the pulse is born above the cap at (0, 2.2, 0) (scale 0→1, 0.6s pulsePop) then slides onto the wire start (0, 1.28, 0); dialog card pops at +0.3s.

**Reduced motion**: curtain replaced by a 0.6s opacity fade; h1 exit-scale skipped; wave loop off.

The finale→restart path never reuses the curtain (once-per-arrival moment): `RUN IT AGAIN` uses the 1.4s pulseFade screen fade instead.

sections.name: States 1–5 — The journey (the FSM)
sections.spec:
**Hand-rolled FSM** (`src/worlds/04-pulse/fsm.ts`, ~90 lines, zero libraries): states `poster | reveal | travel(n) | station(n) | finale`; events `START | ARRIVED | NEXT | AGAIN | EXIT`. Guard table (unguarded events are dropped silently):

| state | START | NEXT | AGAIN | EXIT | ARRIVED (internal) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| poster | →reveal→station(1) | — | — | — | — |
| travel(n) | — | — | — | →poster (1.4s fade) | →station(n) |
| station(1–4) | — | →travel(n+1) | — | →poster | — |
| station(5) | — | →finale | — | →poster | — |
| finale | — | — | →station(1) (1.4s fade) | →poster | — |

**Transition grammar** mirrors the measured `walk → cameraEnter → dialog → cameraExit`: NEXT at station(n) → dialog exits (0.45s pulseExit) → camera lerps back to follow pose → `travel(n+1)`: pulse rides the wire at **3 u/s** (measured walk speed), follow-cam fov 40 at pulse+(0,8,8), per-frame lerp **1−0.96^(60·dt)** (measured), lookAt pulse. On arrival (<0.1u): `ARRIVED` → cameraEnter lerps to the authored pose at **1−0.94^(60·dt)** (lands ≈1.1s) → station beat plays → dialog pops **0.6s pulsePop, delay 0.3s after camera settles**.

**Wire**: CatmullRomCurve3 through (0,0.6,0)→(6,0.6,−3)→(12,0.6,−4)→(18,0.6,0)→(24,0.6,3)→(30,0.6,1)→(36,0.6,−3)→(42,0.6,−2)→(48,0.6,0); stations sit on curve points 0/2/4/6/8; ~12u between stations ≈ 4s travel. Pulse travel height y=1.28 (wire y0.6 + tube r0.18 + pulse r0.5).

**Station table** (camera pos → lookAt target; beats are exact choreography):

| # | Name | Element at | Camera pos → target | Beat on arrival |
|---|------|-----------|---------------------|------------------------|
| 1 | PRESS | (0,0,0) | (−3.5, 3.2, 6.5) → (0, 1.1, 0) | (curtain path only) cap self-press births the pulse |
| 2 | SIGNAL | (12,0,−4) | (9, 2.6, 5.5) → (12, 1.4, −4) | pulse arcs through the arch over 0.8s (parabola apex +1.6u, pulsePop); arch flexes scaleY 1.06 (0.6s pulsePop) as it passes; pulse lands on-wire 1.5u past arch center |
| 3 | SPRING | (24,0,3) | (21, 3.4, 7) → (24, 2.2, 3) | pulse drops onto the red platform; spring scaleY 1→0.75 (0.25s power2.in), overshoots 1.12 (0.35s), settles 1.0 (0.9s pulsePop); payload + pulse launched +1.5u on the overshoot, land with squash scaleY 0.8→1 (0.3s pulsePop) |
| 4 | SETTLE | (36,0,−3) | (33.5, 4.2, 5.5) → (36, 0.9, −3) | pulse hops into the cradle bowl (0.5s arc, squash on land); 3 halo tori ripple scale 1→1.25→0.02 staggered 0.15s and flatten over 1.8s total (pulseFade) |
| 5 | SHIP | (48,0,0) | (44, 2.8, 7.5) → (48, 2.4, 0) | pulse accelerates through the 3 compositor panes (each flashes opacity +0.2 for 0.3s as it crosses) into the screen face (pulse z-scale 0.1 + fade, 0.4s); face flashes white→pink; the 16×9 pixel grid cascades fully lit over 0.8s (row order from mulberry32(4)) |

**Dialog copy** (exact; voice = friendly-institutional pop, numbers do the bragging):
- S1 · eyebrow `STATION 01 · PRESS` · title `300 GRAMS OF FORCE` · body `Your thumb lands, the cap dips two millimeters, a switch closes in the dark. A tiny event is born with your name on it. That's the whole miracle — the rest is delivery.` · button `FOLLOW IT`
- S2 · `STATION 02 · SIGNAL` · `RIDING THE WIRE` · `The event sprints up the tree shouting its coordinates. Listeners lean over the track; one of them — yours — snags it mid-air and asks for a state change.` · `KEEP UP`
- S3 · `STATION 03 · SPRING` · `OVERSHOOT IS A FEELING` · `Stiffness 170, damping 26. The value flies past its target on purpose, swings back, and forgives itself. That wobble is the difference between alive and obedient.` · `AND THEN?`
- S4 · `STATION 04 · SETTLE` · `HALF A PIXEL OF CALM` · `The rings tighten until the motion is smaller than anyone can see. Sixteen milliseconds a frame, every frame, until rest is official.` · `ALMOST HOME`
- S5 · `STATION 05 · SHIP` · `HELLO, PIXEL` · `Through the compositor's glass and onto the screen: one state change, painted as light. Door to door in about the blink of a hummingbird.` · `FINISH THE TOUR`

**Reduced motion**: travel states become jump cuts (teleport + 0.3s fade); beats play as instant end-states; idle bobs off.

sections.name: Dialog cards & wayfinding
sections.spec:
**Card anatomy** (z20, ONE reusable DOM node re-filled per station): width 420px, fixed left 48px bottom 48px (≤800: left 16 right 16 bottom 16, width auto); background #fff, radius 24px, padding 32px, box-shadow `0 24px 48px rgb(48 44 53 / 35%)`. Contents: eyebrow 13px/600/+3.5px/uppercase in #e5262c; title 32px/800/ls −1px/uppercase/lh 0.95 in #3d3c47, margin-top 12px (≤960: 28px); body 17px/300/lh 1.5 in #3d3c47, margin-top 16px; NEXT pill margin-top 24px, **h 54px**, radius 44px, pad 0 32px, 16px/700/+1.4px/uppercase, red `::before` fill (scale 1.05 hover, 200ms), white text. Identical in both themes — the white card is the constant.

**Motion**: pop in `scale 0.9→1, y 24→0, autoAlpha 0→1`, 0.6s pulsePop, delay 0.3s after camera settle; exit `scale→0.92, y→24, autoAlpha→0`, 0.45s pulseExit; text swap happens at exit-complete. GSAP owns all card transforms; the card carries zero CSS transitions.

**Progress dots** (z10, fixed bottom 24px centered row; **≤800: fixed top 20px centered** — bottom collides with the sheet-style dialog): 5 × 8px circles, gap 12px; idle #fdd2d2 at 40%; visited 100% pink; active white + GSAP scale 1.4 pop (0.6s pulsePop). During travel no dot is active; on ARRIVED the new dot pops. Dots are `<button aria-label="Station N — NAME">`: clicking a *visited* dot jumps via the 1.4s pulseFade (no travel replay); unvisited dots inert (`aria-disabled`). Visited set resets on RUN IT AGAIN.

**The hanging tag doubles as the progress meter** (see 2D assets): keycap fill level rises **6.15% → 26.15% → 46.15% → 66.15% → 86.15% → 100%** — station 3 lands exactly on the measured 46.15/46.17% hard cut; GSAP animates both gradient stop offsets together, 0.6s pulseFade per arrival.

**Keyboard**: global keydown — Enter/Space dispatches START/NEXT/AGAIN per state, BUT if `document.activeElement` is a button or link, the handler returns and lets native activation fire (no double-trigger). Esc = EXIT from any non-poster state. Focus rings: 3px #fdd2d2 outline, offset 3px, on all pills/dots/roundel/toggle. Dialog container is `aria-live="polite"`; focus is never stolen (the global keys are the interface).

sections.name: State 6 — Finale (the one green moment)
sections.spec:
On S5 NEXT: dialog exits; camera pulls to the god-pose **(24, 16, 26) → target (24, 1.5, 0)** at lerp **1−0.95^(60·dt)** (≈1.9s) — the whole 48u machine reads as one poster composition (the machine's ends intentionally bleed off-canvas at 16:9; graphic crop, not a framing bug). Simultaneously the confetti burst fires from the screen slab at (48, 2.4, 0): one InstancedMesh, 80 rounded quads, instance colors #fff/#fdd2d2/#e5262c, velocities from **mulberry32(4)** — vx ∈ [−3,3], vy ∈ [4,8], vz ∈ [−2,2], gravity −9, life 1.2s, then mesh hidden. DOM finale overlay (z25) fades in 1.4s pulseFade over the live scene — no curtain, ever.

**Overlay** (same left-96px block grid as the poster, transparent ground — the hall shows through; white on the plum hall holds ≥7:1 contrast in both themes):
- The stamp: 96×96 hand-drawn SVG check-in-circle, stroke 8px round caps, drawn on via stroke-dashoffset (circle 0.45s then check 0.35s, power2.out) in **#00b870 — the world's only green, this is its one moment**. Nothing else may ever be green.
- Eyebrow, 16px/600/+3.5px, white: `TOUR COMPLETE`
- H1, 96px/800/lh 0.9/ls −5px/uppercase, two spans white/pink: `THAT WAS` / `ONE CLICK.`
- Body, 18px/300, max-width 380px: `Every tap you make today takes this exact trip. Now you know what you're asking for.`
- Pill row, margin-top 48px, gap 16px: `RUN IT AGAIN` (h 54px, white fill/red text; night red fill/white text) + `BACK TO THE LAB` (ghost: transparent, 2px border rgb(255 255 255 / 40%), white text, h 54px, radius 44px, pad 0 32px; hover border→white 200ms; href=/).

Entrance stagger on the 300ms grid: stamp 0s, eyebrow 0.3s, h1 lines 0.6/0.9s (pulsePop), body+pills 1.2s (fades). `RUN IT AGAIN`: tag fill back to 6.15% (0.6s), visited dots reset, pulse teleports to S1, 1.4s pulseFade into station(1); the stamp re-draws on the next finale — still the single green slot.

sections.name: Furniture — roundel, tag, toggle, exits
sections.spec:
All inside `#furniture` z30, persistent across every state.

**Roundel badge** (fixed top-right, 24px inset): **149×149px** (measured; ≤800: 96px). `<button aria-label="Return to start">` — clicking = EXIT to poster. Disc filled `#e5272c` (SVG red) with 2px white inner ring at r70; circular ring text at r58 — `PRESS · SIGNAL · SPRING · SETTLE · SHIP · ` in live SVG `<textPath>` (Outfit 700, 12px, +2px tracking, white) with **textLength="364" lengthAdjust="spacing"** so the ring closes exactly (2π·58 = 364.4) regardless of font metrics. Rotation: **CSS `rotate 360deg / 8s linear infinite`** on the ring group only — CSS owns this transform exclusively, GSAP never touches it; `prefers-reduced-motion` freezes it. Center glyph (static): fingertip-on-pill — 44×20 r10 white rounded rect + descending pink #fdd2d2 finger capsule; CSS keyframe presses the finger translateY 3px every 4s (150ms down, 350ms back).

**Hanging tag** (desktop only, hidden ≤960; hangs from the viewport top at **left 62%** — the reference's bag hangs right-of-center; left-120 would collide with the copy block): SVG 200×300, flat-vector language (no strokes-as-outlines, flat fills, chunky radii): cord = 6×40 r3 rect at x97, fill #302c35 day / **#fdd2d2 night** (plum-on-plum would vanish on the night poster); hook 16×10 r4 at (92,36), same swap; tag body x36 y52 w128 h168 r26 fill **#fdd2d2** (pink body so the white keycap reads in both themes); grommet at (100,76): circle r8 #3d3c47 + punch circle r4.5 #fdd2d2 (layered fills, no stroke); keycap x56 y96 w88 h88 r20, fill = vertical `linearGradient` with **two stops at P% / P+0.02%** — below: `#e5272c` (the fill), above: `#fff` — P animated as the journey meter (6.15→26.15→46.15→66.15→86.15→100); shadow ellipse cx100 cy192 rx32 ry5 fill #f3c1c3; label `ONE CLICK` centered y216, Outfit 800, 13px, +1.5px tracking, #3d3c47 (on the pink body — never under the fill). Idle swing: GSAP `rotation −2.5 ↔ +2.5`, 3.2s, sine.inOut, yoyo, repeat −1, transformOrigin '50% −20px' (GSAP owns it; zero CSS transitions on the tag).

**Theme toggle** (fixed top-left, 24px inset): 54×54 mini pushbutton — outer ring #3d3c47 day / white 20% night; inner 40px white cap with a hand-drawn glyph morphing sun↔moon (sun = 12px disc + 8 chunky r2 rounded rays; moon = same disc masked by an offset circle; GSAP scaleX on the mask circle, 0.4s pulsePop). Press: cap dips scale 0.86 in 150ms, then the 800ms cubic-bezier(0.45,0,0.55,1) theme cross-fade (hub curve) while the 3D scene retunes (centerpiece table). Persists to localStorage 'hub-theme'.

**Exit link**: poster + finale only (CSS-hidden mid-journey via `body[data-state]`; Esc/roundel are the mid-tour exits): ghost pill fixed bottom-right 24px, h 40px, radius 44, pad 0 20px, 13px/700/+1.4px/uppercase, 2px border white 40%, white text: `← BACK TO THE LAB`, href=/.

centerpiece: THE MACHINE HALL — one continuous 48-unit toy machine on a plum ground, built entirely from filleted primitives (the anti-Sundial: graphic forms with real craft, no photography cosplay, no literal miniature diorama). Renderer: vanilla Three.js WebGLRenderer (the reference runs WebGPU; we consciously stay WebGL for reach), antialias on, dpr = min(devicePixelRatio, 1.75), **NeutralToneMapping** (ACES hue-shifts this red — the Sundial lesson applied to #e5262c), outputColorSpace sRGB, clearColor **0x4b4a53** day / **0x302c35** night (the measured canvas-into-plum blend). MATERIAL LAW — seven shared MeshStandardMaterials, roughness 0.35, metalness 0, plus unlit basics for signal elements: `matRed` #e5262c (S1 cap, arch, S3 platform) · `matPink` #f9cfd1 (spring, cradle bowl) · `matPlumDeep` #302c35 day / #262230 night (S1 base, wire tube, footings, S5 slab) · `matWhite` (payload, pulse shell) · `matGround` #46454f day / #38363f night · unlit: MeshBasicMaterial #fdd2d2 (chevrons, heat tail additive 45%, pixel grid via instanceColor), white-translucent basics for tori/panes. One PMREM RoomEnvironment environment, envMapIntensity **0.25 day / 0.15 night** — the difference between clay and product; generated once at init. GEOMETRY (all radii are fillets, nothing sharp): [1] Ground: 120u circle, matGround, seeded-speckle map, receiveShadow. [2] The pulse (protagonist): 0.5r sphere, white shell + emissive #fdd2d2 intensity **1.2 day / 2.2 night**, plus one additive 128px canvas glow sprite (scale 2.2u/0.55 opacity day, 3u/0.8 night), castShadow. [3] S1 button: lathe base r2.4 h0.8 matPlumDeep + lathe cap r2.0 h0.9 with 0.25 fillet profile matRed + white inset ring. [4] Wire: one TubeGeometry along the full CatmullRom path, r0.18, matPlumDeep + InstancedMesh of 60 chevron quads (MeshBasic #fdd2d2, unlit so they read as signal at night) spaced 0.8u, advancing 0.12 u/s, matrix update per frame, ONE draw — plus **24 instanced pylon capsules** (r0.12, h0.6, matPlumDeep) under the wire every ~2u so travel never crosses empty ground (1 draw). [5] Heat tail: additive capsule r0.3 len1.6 aligned to the curve tangent 0.8u behind the pulse, visible only during travel (1 draw). [6] S2 listener arch: half-torus r3 tube 0.35 matRed + merged footings (BufferGeometryUtils.mergeGeometries). [7] S3 spring: helix TubeGeometry (5 coils, r1.2, tube 0.22, 200 tubular segs) matPink + red platform disc + white RoundedBox payload 1.4³ r0.2 — the spring physically compresses 0.75, overshoots 1.12, settles (backOut made of geometry). [8] S4 cradle: lathe bowl r2 matPink + 3 concentric halo tori (MeshBasic white, opacity 0.6/0.45/0.3, depthWrite false, renderOrder 5/6/7). [9] S5 screen: RoundedBox slab 6×4×0.6 r0.15 matPlumDeep + face plane 5.4×3.4 basic #f9cfd1 + InstancedMesh 16×9 pixel quads (0.28² gap 0.06, instanceColor plum-dark base, lit #fdd2d2; idle 2–3 pixels flicker on a mulberry32(4) schedule) + 3 compositor panes (RoundedBox 3×2×0.05 at z 1.2/1.8/2.4, MeshBasic white opacity 0.35/0.5/0.65, depthWrite false, renderOrder 10/11/12). [10] Finale confetti: one InstancedMesh, 80 quads, hidden until fired. castShadow = pulse, button base+cap, arch, spring+payload, bowl, slab, pylons (11 casters); castShadow FALSE for tori, panes, sprite, chevrons, pixels, wire, tail, ring. DRAW CALLS: steady 26 visible (confetti hidden) / 27 during travel; **shadowMap.autoUpdate = false with a dirty flag** (Sundial hygiene — shadow re-renders only during travel, beats, theme retune: 11 casters → worst frame 38, inside the ≤40 budget; idle frames stay at 26). LIGHTS: ONE directional shadow light (the measured rule) at pulse+(8,14,6), intensity 2.2 day / 0.9 night, 1024 shadow map, frustum ±10u tracking the pulse (light.target = pulse), bias −0.0005, normalBias 0.02; hemisphere fill (sky #fdd2d2 → ground #302c35) 0.35 day / 0.15 night; **night-only PointLight parented to the pulse** (#fdd2d2, intensity 0 day / ~20 night, distance 14, decay 2 — tune so the ground under the pulse reads ≈#6a5570) making the night promise literal: the protagonist IS the light. CAMERA: fov 40; follow pose pulse+(0,8,8), per-frame lerp 1−0.96^(60·dt) (measured); cameraEnter 1−0.94^(60·dt) (~1.1s); finale pull 1−0.95^(60·dt) (~1.9s); travel 3 u/s (measured). INTERACTIONS: the FSM drives everything — no free orbit; pointer adds ±0.4u parallax (lerp 0.05) at stations only. THEME RETUNE on toggle (all lerped over the same 800ms): clearColor, matGround color + speckle canvas redraw (needsUpdate), matPlumDeep color, directional 2.2↔0.9, hemisphere 0.35↔0.15, pulse emissive 1.2↔2.2, point light 0↔20, envMapIntensity 0.25↔0.15, glow sprite 0.55↔0.8. HYGIENE: rAF paused on document.visibilitychange AND IntersectionObserver on the canvas (gsap.globalTimeline pauses with it); webglcontextlost → preventDefault, body.is-fallback (canvas display:none; the layer beneath is already red/plum — no white flash); contextrestored → re-init renderer/scene and resume at the current FSM state.

motion: GSAP throughout; GSAP owns every transform it ever touches — those elements carry zero CSS transitions (the hub's stranded-entrance lesson). The ONLY CSS-animated transforms are the roundel ring rotation, the roundel finger press, and pill ::before scaling — none of which GSAP touches. EASES via three CustomEase registrations (GSAP 3.13+ all-free): **pulsePop** = cubic-bezier(.34,1.56,.64,1) (the measured backOut), **pulseExit** = cubic-bezier(.36,0,.66,−1.2) (the measured anticipation bezier — every element leaves by dipping against its exit direction first), **pulseFade** = cubic-bezier(.42,0,.58,1) (framer's exact easeInOut — NOT power1.inOut — for the measured 1.4s screen fades). VOCABULARY (all delays quantized to 0/0.3/0.6/0.9/1.2s): screen fade = 1.4s pulseFade (finale overlay, dot-jumps, Esc, RUN IT AGAIN); curtain = 2s linear, once, with the 1s-loop wave strip; pop = 0.6s pulsePop (dialog cards, h1 lines, dots, arch flex, pulse birth, squash returns); exit = 0.45s pulseExit (dialogs, poster copy); press = 150ms cap-dip (scaleY 0.82 / scale 0.86) + 0.35s pulsePop return (S1 button, theme toggle; CTA ::before active state 60ms). 3D CONTINUOUS (per-frame lerp, never tweened): follow-cam 1−0.96^(60·dt) (measured); cameraEnter 1−0.94^(60·dt) ≈1.1s; finale pull 1−0.95^(60·dt) ≈1.9s; pointer parallax lerp 0.05 (stations only); travel 3 u/s (measured walk speed); chevron drift 0.12 u/s. IDLE (subtle, measured-anatomy scale): pulse bob ±0.15u, 1.6s sine.inOut yoyo while waiting at stations; tag swing ±2.5°, 3.2s sine.inOut yoyo, transformOrigin '50% −20px'; pixel-grid flicker on the seeded schedule; roundel 8s CSS rotation; roundel finger press every 4s. ENTRANCES: poster/finale copy staggers on the 300ms grid — pulsePop for h1 lines, plain 0.6s fades for eyebrow/body/pills; stamp dashoffset circle 0.45s then check 0.35s power2.out. HOVER: pill ::before scale 1.05 in 200ms ease-out; ghost-pill border-color 200ms. THEME CHANGE: DOM cross-fade 800ms cubic-bezier(0.45,0,0.55,1) (the hub's exact curve) with all 3D retunes lerped on the same clock, preceded by the 150ms cap-dip. prefers-reduced-motion: travel → jump-cut + 0.3s fade; curtain → 0.6s fade; all idles off (roundel rotation frozen); dashoffset draws become instant; station beats render as end-states.
fallback: Four-rung ladder, each rung art-directed, and html/body is ALWAYS themed (red or hall-plum) so no rung can ever flash white. [1] LIVE (real GPU): the full journey as specced. [2] SOFTWARE RENDERER (WEBGL_debug_renderer_info matches SwiftShader/llvmpipe/software): no rAF loop — the journey becomes a click-through SLIDESHOW of designed stills: on every FSM state change, place the pulse at its station rest pose, set the authored camera pose, render exactly ONE frame at dpr 1 (one software render per click is affordable; travel states are skipped as cuts). Shadows off, hemisphere boosted to 0.6 to compensate. Curtain, dialogs, dots, tag, roundel, toggle all still run — they're DOM. [3] NO WEBGL / CONTEXT LOST (context creation fails, or webglcontextlost fires: preventDefault + body.is-fallback, canvas display:none; on contextrestored, re-init and resume at current state): the FSM survives as a 2D diagram journey — the five 96×96 flat-vector station glyphs joined by a 3px dashed plum/pink line (720px horizontal strip centered; ≤800: vertical 5-stop stack) replaces the hall; a 16px pink pulse dot hops glyph-to-glyph via GSAP (0.9s pulsePop per hop), the active glyph pops scale 1.15; dialog cards, copy, dots, tag meter and theming are identical to live. Still a guided tour, not an apology. [4] STILL FRAME (first paint / shares / no-JS): the poster state IS a complete flat composition — themed ground, two-tone stack, pill, roundel, tag — painted by HTML+CSS before any JS runs (blocking inline theme script guarantees scheme-correct first paint); export it as the og-image; noscript visitors get the poster plus its one-line machine apology.
distinct: Pulse is the only surface in the lab with no scroll at all — a click-through state machine where the page itself is the button — and the only one committed to a single saturated hue: red #e5262c IS the canvas, not an accent. The hub is warm cream paper with Cabinet Grotesk, toy-box color cards, and a painted-wood sundial relief; Noir is charcoal-and-bone night cinema with 10px mono chips and power4/expo restraint; Chrome is greige editorial serif with liquid metal; Monument is a white void of colossal hairline-sliced caps. Pulse shares a family with none of them: ONE variable font (Outfit) doing every job by weight alone (800/700/600/300, 400/500 forbidden), two-tone white/pink stacked headlines, pill-and-roundel furniture, backOut/anticipation cartoon physics on a 300ms delay grid, a hanging tag that is secretly a progress meter, and a filleted toy machine you ride station by station behind a one-time linear curtain with a red wave edge. If a screenshot shows red ground, pink second lines, a rotating roundel, and a white dialog card with a NEXT pill — it can only be World 04.
